events.text: {npc} of the Star Sea Listeners finds you on the rim of a drifting isle at night, counting stars because you cannot afford a lamp. "You counted the falling ones too," {he} says. "Most people only count the pretty ones. Count for us. We pay in spirit stones, and in charts you will never be allowed to copy."

effects.log: The lens is cold and very old. Through it every immortal on the isle wears a faint second light, like a price. You are a star listener.

choices.text: Ask who the charts are for

effects.log: "The Celestial Ministries, first," {npc} says. "Whoever pays after them, second."

events.text: The stall-keeper {npc} sells you a paper lantern on the Drifting Isles for one spirit stone, then charges a second stone to tell you where it was made. "Everything in the Lantern Market is sold twice," {he} says. "Once to the buyer, once to whoever wants to know what the buyer bought. You have good ears. Rent them to me."

effects.log: {npc} hangs your lantern over {his} stall as a sign. Whoever walks past it is your business now. You are a stall runner of the Lantern Market.
{npc} is delighted. "A runner who haggles listens to prices," {he} says, and pays a little more than you asked, which worries you.

events.text: A grey feather settles on your sleeve over a cloud strait with no birds in it. Then {npc} is standing beside you, smelling of cold ash. "The Ashen Wing does not pay in stones," {he} says. "Stones are what the Jade Court counts. We count debts. Carry our ears, and one day we will carry you somewhere nobody else will go."

effects.log: {npc} nods once and steps off into the cloud. The feather is warm and never burns. You are a grey feather of the Ashen Wing.

choices.text: Ask what the debt will be

effects.log: "Small," says {npc}. "They always are, at first."

events.text: {npc} meets you on the jade stairs below the Court, where everyone climbing is too busy being seen to see anything. {He} reads your report and folds it into a paper crane, which flies off over the clouds. "Somebody very old will read that tonight," {he} says. "Do not wonder who."

effects.log: You manage it for nearly a year.
It flies toward the Jade Court, then turns at the last moment toward somewhere else. {npc} sees you watching.

events.text: Your drop is a hollow in an old pine on a drifting isle. This year the isle drifted, pine and all, three days east. {npc} found it anyway, and left your stones with a note: next time, pick a tree that stays put.

effects.log: {npc} approves of the rock. "Rocks are loyal," {he} writes.
"I listen for trees," {npc} says, which explains nothing at all.

events.text: {npc} has a cold, which immortals are not supposed to get, and sneezes every time you say the name of a sect. "A curse," {he} says. "A small one. Somebody disliked a report of mine. Be careful which of yours you sign."

effects.log: {npc} drinks it, sneezes less, and as thanks tells you who cursed {him}. It is very useful.
Your reports go unsigned from now on. {npc} sneezes approvingly.

events.text: {npc} pays you less than last year and does not explain. Then, at the door, {he} mentions that your usual ferry is being watched by a clerk of the Ministry of Rites, and that it would be a shame to lose a good ear to a bad ferry.

effects.log: The warning was worth more than the missing stones. {npc} knows you know it.
{npc} pays them to the last chip, and warns you about nothing for a while.

events.text: {npc} hands you a brass tube with a chart sealed inside. "You carry now, between the isles," {he} says. "The seal is a thread of spirit. If it is broken when it lands, we will know, and so will you, for about a day."

choices.text: Swear never to break a seal

effects.log: {npc} believes you, which is either kind or very clever. You are {inw_rank}.

choices.text: Ask what happens after the day

effects.log: "You find out what you carried," {npc} says, "the hard way."

events.text: {npc} gives you an isle. Not to own: to hear. Three ferries, a pine forest, the outer court of a sect, and every whisper on it now reaches you before it reaches {him}. "Be fair to your ears," {he} says. "An immortal you underpay has a very long time to resent it."

effects.log: {npc} writes it in a ledger kept since before the isle floated. You are {inw_rank}.

choices.text: Ask what became of the last one

effects.log: "Four thousand good years," {npc} says, "then somebody bought the isle out from under them."

events.text: The elders of {inw_net} meet on a cloud that is only there once a month, around a table cut from one slab of star-iron. {npc} pulls out a chair for you. "From here," {he} says, "you choose which secrets reach the Jade Court and which ones quietly do not."

effects.log: The chair is cold. Your name goes into a book older than most sects. You are {inw_rank}.

choices.text: Look at the head of the table

effects.log: {npc} follows your eyes, smiles, and says nothing at all.

events.text: {npc} has headed {inw_net} since before the present Sovereign took the Jade Throne. {He} sets two cups of cloud tea on the table and pushes one to you. "Half my elders want you in my chair," {he} says. "The other half want to see who wins. Which half are you in?"

choices.text: Say you will take it, if it comes to that

effects.log: {npc} drinks {his} tea to the bottom. "Then it comes to that," {he} says, and stands.

choices.text: Say the chair is {his} while {he} wants it

effects.log: {npc} looks at you a long time. "Correct," {he} says. "And I believe about half of it."

events.text: The elders come to you one at a time, on different clouds, each asking the same question in a different robe: how many more thousand years does old {npc} mean to sit? Immortals are patient. Elders are less patient than they look.

choices.text: Go to {npc} openly and ask for the chair

effects.log: You send word that you will come at dawn, alone, by the front door. It is the most frightening letter you have ever written.
{npc} hears of it by evening. A jar of thousand-year wine arrives at your door with no note.

events.text: {npc} gives you the seal of {inw_net} with both hands: a grey stone worn smooth by more thumbs than anyone counted. "I held it eleven thousand years," {he} says. "Do not hold it so long. Nobody should know this much for that long."

choices.text: Promise to hand it on in time

effects.log: {npc} walks out onto the cloud without a guard for the first time in eleven thousand years, and seems lighter. You are {inw_rank}.
"Everyone," {npc} says.

events.text: The old head of {inw_net} left a sealed letter and a pine seedling in a clay pot. The elders read the letter in silence, then turn to you. It names you. It also asks, rather firmly, that somebody water the seedling. You are {inw_rank}.

effects.log: The elders watch you water a pine before you give one order. It becomes a story they tell every new ear.

choices.text: Give the first order: change every drop

effects.log: Within a month every drop, sign and courier is new. The elders nod, and one of them quietly waters the pine.

events.text: {inw_net} is, so far, a rented room on an isle that drifts the wrong way, one lamp, a cracked jade slip for records and one ear: an old ferry pilot who knows every strait. "Rogues with no backing are the ones nobody bothers to watch," the pilot says cheerfully. "Where do we start?"

effects.log: By the season's end you know who crossed which strait, and that one sect elder crosses at night with no lamp.
Three other networks, it turns out, and all of them know your name already. The pilot is impressed.

events.text: You hang a paper star in the window of {inw_net}, the old sign that a listening house is open. By morning two jade slips are tucked under the door. One asks your prices. The other says, in a beautiful hand: welcome, little ring. We have been listening to you for a while.

effects.log: Your first client pays in spirit stones of a very old cut, and gives no name.
You keep it. The hand matches nobody you know, which is the point of it.

events.text: {npc} rows a cloud ferry across the Strait of Nine Pines forty times a day, for spirit stones so small they are nearly dust. "People talk on ferries," {he} says. "They think the ferryman is part of the boat."

effects.log: {npc} weighs the stones and grins. Your first ferry is listening.
{npc} starts counting words out loud, which is going to be a problem.

events.text: {npc} is a junior clerk of the Ministry of Records at the Jade Court who copies petitions all day and never forgets a face. {He} also owes a great many spirit stones to a pill-seller, and is too proud to say so.

effects.log: {npc} hears of it from the pill-seller and bows so low you cannot see {his} face. A clerk who owes you is worth three who are paid.

choices.text: Offer a wage, and say nothing of the debt

effects.log: {npc} takes the wage and keeps the debt. {He} is careful with you, and careful is useful.

events.text: {npc} was an outer disciple of a great immortal sect for twelve hundred years and never once let into the inner court. {He} still knows every gate, every guard's turn and which elders refuse to speak. {He} still wears the sect's robe, out of habit.

effects.log: {npc} smiles for the first time in a long while. The robe opens doors.
{npc} burns it. {He} works well and never quite forgives you.

events.text: {npc} keeps a stall in the Lantern Market that opens only after the last lantern is lit, selling things on no list: pills with no maker, maps of isles that sank, and, for the right buyer, who bought what yesterday.

effects.log: {npc}'s hand leaves a glitter of star dust on your palm that will not wash off for a week.

choices.text: Warn {him} not to sell to anyone else

effects.log: {npc} looks wounded, which is how you know {he} was about to.

events.text: {npc} wants a season off. {He} has listened at the same pine for six hundred years and says the pine has started listening back. You suspect a joke. You are not entirely sure.

effects.log: {npc} comes back rested, with a new pine and an old name: the one who had been watching {him}.
{npc} keeps listening. {His} reports begin to describe the pine's moods.

events.text: A sect has offered {npc} three times what you pay, in good stones of the old cut. {He} lays the offer on your table, a sealed jade slip, and does not open it. "I am showing you," {he} says, "so you know what I am worth."

effects.log: It costs you dearly. {npc} keeps the slip unopened, a reminder to you both.

choices.text: Remind {him} of the things you know

fail.log: {npc} stays, and starts keeping a ledger of {his} own about you.

events.text: {npc} has a student: a young fox spirit who swept the ferry dock, saw too much and asked {npc} what it meant. Now the child follows {him} everywhere with a notebook. The child is quick, and also very young, even for a fox.

effects.log: The fox sweeps your back room and remembers every word said in it. A second ear for the price of a bowl of plums.

choices.text: Say the work is too dangerous for a child

effects.log: {npc} takes the child back to the dock. {He} is quieter with you for a long while.

events.text: {npc} has watched an alchemist of the Nine Clouds Palace for a year and has fallen, by {his} own account, completely in love with the alchemist's pills. {He} has eaten six. {His} reports are now very cheerful and faintly glowing.

choices.text: Take {him} off the job and pay a healer

effects.log: The healer costs a fortune and {npc} stops glowing. {He} is grateful, and a little sorry.

choices.text: Tell {him} to keep watching and eat no more

effects.log: {npc} keeps watching. {He} eats one more, and you can tell from the reports.

events.text: {npc} brings you a rumour {he} bought with {his} own stones: a sect elder, a sealed cloud-boat, a date. It is the best thing your ears have brought in all year, and {he} only wants the stones back. Two other ears are watching to see what you pay.

effects.log: {npc} buys new boots and tells every ferry where the stones came from. It is good for business, and bad for quiet.
{npc} nods. Fair is fair. The other ears note it, and bring you less.

events.text: Your ears watched {npc} for a season: how {he} breathes on the jade stairs, how long {he} holds a sword form, which way {he} steps when startled. It arrives as a star chart, every light a habit. You know now how strong {npc} really is.

effects.log: It is on {npc}'s page in your People list now, and nowhere else.
You roll it into a tube. It is the most honest picture of {npc} anyone owns.

events.text: "{npc} trains on a far isle before the sun comes up through the clouds," the report says. "The art {he} shows the Court is a polite one. The art {he} trains is not." Your ear sketched every form from a cloud a mile off.

effects.log: You know what {npc} really carries now.

choices.text: Go and watch one morning yourself

effects.log: You watch from a cloud, cold and damp. The report was exact.

events.text: The second report on {npc} is about what {he} wants: the friends {he} keeps, the grudges {he} has nursed for three thousand years, the one person {he} writes to and never sends the letters. There is a page about you. It is honest.

effects.log: You know {npc} better than {his} own house does now.
You skip it. You read it that night, twice.

events.text: Your ear brings the report on {npc} in person, which ears never do. "{He} has been asking which isle you sleep on," they say, "and which ferry you take, and whether you drink alone. It is not friendship."

effects.log: You sleep somewhere new and dull. {npc} keeps asking.
You sit in {npc}'s hall and talk about the weather for an hour. {He} understands every word.

events.text: The last report on {npc} was never meant to exist. Your ear hands it over folded very small, sealed in the wax of three different sects. Everything {npc} has hidden for ten thousand years is in it.

effects.log: A secret kept can still be sold, or used, or forgiven. You have not decided which.

choices.text: Burn it past the first line

effects.log: You burn it. You remember the first line anyway, which is the trouble with first lines.

events.text: Your people have found the thing {npc} would give an isle to keep buried. They lay it on your table and wait, because what they really came to learn tonight is what kind of master you are.

choices.text: Say nothing will be done with it, yet

effects.log: They nod and go. Yet is a word immortals understand very well.
They smile. Now they know what kind of house this is.

events.text: Your people come back from {inw_house} with frost in their hair and its back halls drawn from memory: who quarrels, what the treasury holds, which elder takes a cloud out alone at night. The last page is a door your ear could not open, a vault sealed in very old ice, and the sound of slow breathing behind it.

effects.log: The dossier goes into the ledger chest under the house's name. The last page you read twice.

choices.text: Ask what the breathing sounded like

effects.log: "Patient," your ear says. "Like something asleep a long time, and in no hurry."

events.text: The gate wardens of {inw_house} were easy. Its steward was not: a three-tailed crane with a long memory who chased your ear across two isles. The books came out anyway, every page copied onto jade slips.

choices.text: Pay the ear for the chase

effects.log: Your ear laughs and winces at once, and spends it on a new robe.

choices.text: Ask if the crane saw a face

effects.log: "Saw a robe," your ear says. "Not a face."

events.text: From outside, {inw_house} is pride and old stones. From inside, your ear reports, it is three branches who have not spoken in eight thousand years, a treasury mostly made of debts, and a portrait in the ancestral hall that someone still dusts every single morning.

effects.log: Nobody in the house will say. They lower their voices near it, as if it might hear.
A house that dusts a portrait every morning is a house expecting someone back. You note it.

events.text: Your ear spent a season as a gardener in the cloud orchards of {inw_house}. The dossier smells of peach blossom: who marries whom next, which branch is quietly selling its spirit veins, and an orchard walk nobody may enter, at the end of which stands a locked pavilion with fresh tea set out every dawn for someone who never comes out.

effects.log: It goes into the ledger chest. You find yourself wondering who the tea is for.

choices.text: Ask whether the tea is ever drunk

effects.log: "Never," your ear says. "They pour it away at dusk, and set out more at dawn."

events.text: The Lantern Market sells a ranking of the strongest immortals for one spirit stone a scroll. Your people followed the names for a year: the one who has not drawn a sword in five thousand years, the one whose famous technique is borrowed, the one ranked tenth who should be second.

effects.log: You could recite it now. You never will.

choices.text: Lock it away for a bad century

effects.log: It goes in the chest. One of those names will come looking for you some day.

events.text: A storyteller on the jade stairs recites the Court's list of great names to a crowd of young immortals, and every rank is wrong. Your ear stands beside you mouthing the true order, and stops when the storyteller looks over.

effects.log: It is a good performance, even if it is a lie.
The crowd turns. The name you corrected will hear of it by morning.

events.text: {npc} sits across from you in a pavilion over the cloud sea and lays a purse of spirit stones on the table, then a second. "I want {inw_house}," {he} says. "Its halls, its quarrels, its treasury. Not the songs the Court sings about it. The truth."

effects.log: {npc} lets go of them. "A thousand years," {he} says. "Not a day more."
{npc} takes them back without a flicker. "There are other ears," {he} says.
"I may be marrying into it," {npc} says, "or ruining it. I have not decided which."

events.text: A crane of folded jade lands on your sill with a letter from {npc}, who does not come in person. It asks for the inner state of {inw_house} and names a price in spirit stones that no honest immortal would offer.

choices.text: Send the crane back with a yes

effects.log: You fold one word into it. It flies off faster than it came.

choices.text: Let the crane go home empty

effects.log: It circles once, offended, and leaves. Some letters should not be answered.

events.text: {npc} is back, and pleased with the last work. {He} wants {inw_house} this time, and adds a handful of stones to the old price. "I like ears that do what they are paid for," {he} says, "and then forget who paid."

effects.log: {npc} pays half in advance, as before.

choices.text: Say your ears are busy this century

effects.log: {npc} shrugs. "Next century, then."

events.text: You hand {npc} the dossier in a plain cloth on the jade stairs. {He} reads the first slip standing, then sits down on a step to read the rest while important immortals walk around {him}. When {he} looks up, {he} is somebody who knows something.

choices.text: Do not ask what {he} will do

effects.log: {npc} pays the rest, and a little more for your silence.
"Better you do not know," {npc} says, "since you already know everything else."

events.text: {npc} pays the second half of the contract in the middle of the Lantern Market, stone by stone, slowly, so every stall-keeper sees that {inw_net} keeps its word.

effects.log: Half the market will want a contract with you by the next moon.

choices.text: Count it again in front of {him}

effects.log: {npc} laughs. The market laughs with {him}. Nobody will cheat you soon.

events.text: A thing only your own people knew is being sold on a slip in the Lantern Market for three stones: a client's name, a price, an isle. Somebody in your house is selling. Every face at the morning meeting looks like a face that could.

effects.log: You watch. The one who sold watches back, and you cannot tell which one it is.
It costs you a season of stones. The leak stops, for a while.

events.text: A courier you have never seen passes you on a cloud ferry and murmurs, very pleasantly, the name of your last client and the price you charged. Then the courier steps off at the next isle. It was not a threat. It was a receipt.

effects.log: You let it go. You count your people again that night.
You lose the courier in the fog of the strait, and find a drop that is not yours.

events.text: {npc} does not deny it. {He} sits in your back room with {his} hands flat on the table. "They said they had my teacher," {he} says, "in a cell under the Ministry of Punishments. Maybe they did. I did not know who else to ask."

effects.log: {npc} stands, bows once, and leaves with nothing but the robe {he} came in.
{npc} puts {his} head on the table and does not lift it for a long time.

choices.text: Keep {him} selling, and write what {he} sells

effects.log: {npc} understands at once. "If they find out," {he} begins, and does not finish.

events.text: You lay the copied slips before {npc} one by one, in the order {he} sold them over four hundred years. {He} watches the pile grow and smiles a little at the end. "I always wondered how long you would take," {he} says. "You are slower than I hoped."

effects.log: {npc} goes laughing, which is somehow worse.
"Naturally," {npc} says. "I sell to whoever is winning, and today it is you."
{npc} stops smiling. Forgiveness was the one thing {he} had not priced.

events.text: Your ear on the Strait of Nine Pines does not come home. The ferry drifts back empty, with the rival's sign laid neatly on the bench. Your ear is gone, taken somewhere you cannot follow, and the whole strait has gone quiet.

choices.text: Search every isle on the strait

effects.log: You search a season and find a scrap of robe and nothing else. Your people saw you search, and they remember.
Your people hear you swear. They work harder after that, and far more carefully.

events.text: You wake to the smell of burning pine. By the time your cloud reaches the safehouse it is ash and one scorched jade slip: a year of listening, a chest of spirit stones, your charts. The fire touched nothing else on the isle. Whoever set it was very careful.

effects.log: You rent a new room before the ash is cold. Your people see that you do not run.
You wait for the heat to pass and the isle to forget the smell of smoke.

events.text: In the crowd on the jade stairs something cold and quick finds the gap between your ribs and your sleeve, and is gone before you turn. A warning, placed exactly. The crowd keeps climbing. Nobody saw anything, which is also a message.

effects.log: You keep climbing, one hand pressed to your side, so whoever is watching sees you keep climbing.
You do not leave your isle for a season.

events.text: {npc}, who speaks for the Star Sea Listeners, sends you a star chart with one star scratched out. It is your star, the one they chart you by. Everyone who reads the sky knows what that means: from tonight the Listeners watch your people, and do worse than watch.

choices.text: Send it back with a new star drawn in

effects.log: {npc} keeps it, which means war anyway, but a respectful one.
Half the Star Sea hears of it before the ash cools.

events.text: Every lantern on {npc}'s row of the Lantern Market goes dark at once, and one is left lit outside your door with a price tag on it. The price is your network. {npc} has decided you are for sale, and that the lantern-sellers are buying.

effects.log: You blow it out. Down among the lanterns, {npc} hears of it, and smiles.

choices.text: Write a higher price on the tag

effects.log: You hang it back on {npc}'s stall. The whole row laughs for a week, and the war starts anyway.

events.text: Your safehouse is full of grey feathers in the morning, hundreds, on every shelf and in every cup, and a slip from {npc}: the Ashen Wing has called in your debt. You were not aware you owed one. With the Ashen Wing, you rarely are.

choices.text: Sweep them out and open as usual

effects.log: Your people see the doors open, and stay.

choices.text: Close the doors for a season

effects.log: You work behind shutters for a season. It is at least quiet.

events.text: The quiet war with {inw_foe} goes on: a courier who never lands, a drop found empty, a warehouse of yours on a drifting isle that drifts, one night, straight into a storm. {npc} sends no slips now. The isles wait to see what you do this year.

effects.log: You give the order.

choices.text: Send {npc} stones and ask for peace

effects.log: You send the stones.

choices.text: Try to turn one of their ears

ok.log: You find one who will listen.

fail.log: The ear you approach goes straight to {npc}.

events.text: {npc} meets you on the jade stairs at noon, the one place in the Upper Realm no network strikes, and offers you a peach from the Court orchards. "We could both stop," {he} says. "Or go on until one of us has no ears left. I have a great many ears. So, I hear, do you."

choices.text: Take the peach, and the peace, at a price

effects.log: You name a price. {npc} names a higher one. You pay it.

choices.text: Drop the peach over the edge

effects.log: It falls a very long way into the clouds. "Then go on," {npc} says.

events.text: Your ears bring you the name of {npc}'s best listener: a robe-maker who fits the elders of half the great houses and hears everything said with arms raised. The robe-maker's apprentice wants a place in a sect the robe-maker cannot afford.

effects.log: The robe-maker starts sewing your slips into the hems.
You give the order. You do not sleep well for a season.

events.text: It ends in a pavilion over the cloud sea. The spymaster of {inw_foe} pours you a cup of cloud tea and leaves without drinking. {inw_net} has won the quiet war, and every stall in the Lantern Market knows it by moonrise.

effects.log: It is excellent tea. Nobody poisons tea in a pavilion the whole Upper Realm is watching.

choices.text: Leave it, and pay for both cups

effects.log: The pavilion sees you pay. That is how the isles learn who won.

events.text: You count your people at the morning meeting and it does not take long. {inw_foe} has the straits now, and the ferries, and one of your safehouses with your sign still painted on the door. Immortals have long memories. So, you tell yourself, do you.

effects.log: You start again. The best networks are always smaller than they look.
Your remaining ears hear you swear it.

events.text: Nobody says the war with {inw_foe} is over. The couriers simply start landing again, and your warehouses stop drifting into storms. It is the kind of peace counted in centuries without anyone going missing.

effects.log: You count the first century. It is a good one.

choices.text: Send their spymaster a jar of wine

effects.log: The jar comes back empty, washed, with a peach stone in it. It is a reply.

events.text: {npc} holds the seal of {inw_net} the way you held it on your first night: much too tight. "What do I do first?" {he} asks, and then, before you can answer, "No. Let me guess."

effects.log: {npc} guesses: change every drop. {He} is right, and you see the head of a network in {his} smile.

choices.text: Tell {him}: forget what you know about me

effects.log: {npc} does not promise. That is how you know you chose well.

events.text: Nobody hears {npc} arrive. One moment you are alone in the hall of your small domain, the next an oracle of the Silent Hall sits beside you mid-sentence, as if you had been talking for an hour. "You remember things," {he} says. "Gods mostly do not bother. The Hall would like to borrow your memory, and pay in prayers nobody else can hear."

effects.log: {npc} touches your brow, and for a moment you remember a conversation you never had. You are a novice oracle.

choices.text: Ask what the Hall does with what it borrows

effects.log: "Keeps it," {npc} says. "Forever. That is rather the point of us."

events.text: At a crossroads between three worlds, a small god with a toll-box and a lantern stops your prayers on their way up and reads one aloud. "Sincere," says {npc}. "A bit long." {He} keeps one prayer in ten. "Every prayer passes a crossroads, and the Choir hears them all. Want to sing with us?"

effects.log: {npc} gives you a toll-box of your own, very small. You are a road spirit of the Choir of the Crossroads.
{npc} hands it back, laughing, and offers you the work anyway.

events.text: A raven lands on the rail of your hall during a thunderstorm in a world below, and the storm stops to let it speak. It is {npc}, of the Ravens of the Storm Throne. "Weather goes everywhere," {he} says. "So do we. Tell us what you see, and the Throne of Storms will remember who told it."

effects.log: {npc} perches. {His} claws are cold as hail. You are a fledgling of the Ravens.

choices.text: Ask what the Throne does with a memory

effects.log: "Weighs it," says {npc}. "The Throne weighs everything."

events.text: {npc} takes your report and drops it into a well that runs through every world at once. Somewhere, a dreamer wakes with the gist of it. "Delivered," {he} says. "Do not ask to whom. The dreamer does not know either."

effects.log: You manage it, mostly. Some nights you dream of the well.
You see a thousand faces looking up before {npc} pulls you back by the collar.

events.text: Your pay this year comes as prayers: the thin, honest prayers of a fishing village in a world you have never seen, routed to you by {npc}. They ask for a calm sea. It is, strictly speaking, now your problem.

effects.log: You spend a little of yourself on a village you will never visit. {npc} notices, and approves.
It is good faith. The village gets its storm anyway, though not from you.

events.text: {npc} is in a terrible mood. A pantheon has spread a rumour that {he} is the god of a minor kind of mildew, and in three worlds people now pray to {him} about bread. "This," {he} says, "is what happens when one of my reports is signed."

effects.log: {npc} cheers up slightly. Your reports go unsigned from now on.

choices.text: Ask whether the mildew prayers pay

effects.log: "Better than you would think," {npc} admits.

events.text: {npc} pays you less than usual and gives no reason. Then, at the door, {he} mentions that a judge of the Heavenly Court has started reading the Book of Fates at the page with your name on it, and that a sensible god would take another road home tonight.

effects.log: The warning was worth more than the missing faith. {npc} knows you know.
{npc} pays it to the last prayer, and warns you of nothing for a while.

events.text: {npc} gives you a small bell that makes no sound. "You carry now, between domains," {he} says. "The bell rings for anyone who opens what you carry, and it rings in the hall of whoever sent it. You will never hear it. They will."

choices.text: Swear never to open a message

effects.log: {npc} believes you, or decides to. You are {inw_rank}.
Nothing. Somewhere very far off, somebody looks up. {npc} sighs.

events.text: {npc} gives you a world to listen to: a small one, round and blue, with three moons and a great many temples. Every prayer it sends now passes through your hands first. "Be fair to your listeners," {he} says. "Starve them, and they start praying to someone else."

effects.log: {npc} writes it in a book with pages thin as breath. You are {inw_rank}.

choices.text: Ask what became of its last listener

effects.log: "Turned into a minor god of its third moon," {npc} says. "Be careful what you come to love."

events.text: The elders of {inw_net} meet in a room that exists only while all of them are thinking of it. {npc} thinks a chair into it for you. "From here," {he} says, "you decide which prayers reach the pantheons and which are quietly answered by nobody."

effects.log: The chair holds, which from that room is a compliment. You are {inw_rank}.
It is the only chair nobody had to think of. It was always there. {npc} sees you looking.

events.text: {npc} has headed {inw_net} since before the pantheons had names. {He} holds out a cup of nectar, just out of your reach. "Half my elders want you in my chair," {he} says. "The other half want to see which way the Book of Fates turns first. Which half are you?"

choices.text: Say you will take the chair, if it comes to that

effects.log: {npc} gives you the cup. "It has come to that," {he} says, and stands.

choices.text: Say the chair is {his} for as long as {he} wants it

effects.log: {npc} drinks your nectar {him}self. "A lovely answer," {he} says. "I believe a third of it."

events.text: The elders come to you in dreams, one a night, each wearing a different face and asking the same thing: how many more ages does old {npc} mean to keep the chair? Gods do not die of age. Some of them retire, if pushed.

choices.text: Go to {npc} awake, and ask openly

effects.log: You send word that you will come at dawn by the front door. Gods rarely use front doors. {npc} will know it is serious.
You sleep without dreaming. {npc} hears of it, and sends you honey from a world that no longer exists.

events.text: {npc} gives you the seal of {inw_net} with both hands: a mirror that shows nothing. "I kept it since the first prayer was said," {he} says. "Do not keep it so long. Nobody should know this much for so long, and gods least of all."

choices.text: Promise to hand it on in time

effects.log: {npc} walks out into the plain daylight of some small world and stays there, pleased, for a hundred years. You are {inw_rank}.
For a moment it shows everyone. Then, kindly, nothing again.

events.text: The old head of {inw_net} has gone quiet the way gods do, past every prayer's reach. The elders set the empty mirror in front of you. Nobody speaks. You are {inw_rank}, and every listener in heaven is waiting for your first word.

choices.text: Say the old head's name aloud

effects.log: You say it, so that at least one prayer still reaches them. The elders weep, which gods rarely do.

choices.text: Order every road and toll changed

effects.log: Within a month every sign of the network is new. The elders nod, satisfied.

events.text: {inw_net} is, so far, one lamp, a borrowed shrine in a world that barely prays, and one listener: a retired god of lost keys who knows every lock in heaven and is delighted to be asked. "Small gods are the ones nobody watches," the god of keys says. "Where do we begin?"

effects.log: By the season's end you know which judge of the Heavenly Court leaves by the back door, and when.
Three other networks, the god of keys reports, and all three already have your name in a book.

events.text: You light a lamp in the window of {inw_net}, the old sign that a listening house is open. By morning two prayers have arrived. One asks your prices. The other uses a name you have never told anyone, and says only: welcome. We hear you too.

effects.log: Your first client pays in old, heavy faith from a world that fell long ago, and gives no name.
You keep it. It is the most frightening prayer you have ever received, and very politely written.

events.text: {npc} is a road spirit on the stair that prayers climb from a hundred worlds, a sort of porter who carries the heavy ones up. "People pray louder than they think," {he} says. "And they pray the truth. Nobody lies to a god on purpose."

effects.log: {npc} tucks the faith in {his} cap and grins. Your first stair is listening.
{npc} starts counting out loud. It will be a long partnership.

events.text: {npc} is a junior gatekeeper of the Heavenly Court who checks names against the Book of Fates at the Third Gate. {He} knows who came in, who left, and who came in under a name the Book does not hold. {He} also owes a great deal of faith to a god of wine.

effects.log: {npc} hears of it from the god of wine and bows so low you cannot see {his} face.

choices.text: Offer a wage, and leave the debt alone

effects.log: {npc} takes the wage and keeps the debt. {He} is careful with you.

events.text: {npc} served a pantheon for an age as the god of its banquet seating, the most political office in heaven. {He} knows who will not sit beside whom, and why, back to the first feast. The pantheon retired {him} for seating two rivals together. On purpose, {he} says.

effects.log: {npc} is thrilled, and draws you a seating plan of all heaven on a napkin.

choices.text: Take {him} on, but ask {him} to stop telling that story

effects.log: {npc} stops telling it. {He} works well, and resents you a little.

events.text: {npc} lives in the dark between domains, where gods go when they do not want to be seen going. {He} keeps no lamp and charges no toll, but remembers every god who passed {him} in the dark, and what they carried.

effects.log: You cannot see it. It is very cold, and it holds on a moment longer than it should.

choices.text: Warn {him} not to sell to anyone else

effects.log: There is a long, offended silence in the dark.

events.text: {npc} has started to be worshipped. A village below glimpsed {him} once while {he} was listening at their shrine, and now they leave {him} bread. {He} is embarrassed, a little thrilled, and has begun answering.

effects.log: {npc} keeps it, and works harder for you out of sheer happiness.

choices.text: Tell {him} an ear cannot be the god of anything

effects.log: {npc} stops answering. The bread keeps coming for a while. Then it stops.

events.text: A pantheon has offered {npc} three times what you pay, in old faith from a famous world. {He} sets the offer on your table, a sealed hymn, and does not open it. "I am showing you," {he} says, "so you know what I am worth to them."

effects.log: It costs you a season of prayers. {npc} keeps the hymn unopened, a reminder to you both.

ok.log: {npc} goes as quiet as the Silent Hall, and stays.

fail.log: {npc} stays, and starts keeping a book about you.

events.text: {npc} has spent a century listening at the dreams of a sleeping goddess of rivers and has begun dreaming those dreams too. {His} reports now arrive soaking wet and describe fish in great detail.

effects.log: {npc} dries out over a season and thanks you, a little sadly. {He} misses the fish.
{npc} keeps listening. The reports get wetter, and much more interesting.

events.text: An old friend of {npc}'s turns up at your shrine: a god of a fallen world with no worshippers left, asking for {npc} by the name from when {he} was still a god of something. Two of your other listeners watch from the rafters to see what you do.

choices.text: Give the friend a prayer and a seat by the fire

effects.log: The friend warms up, and goes. {npc} thanks you without a word.
You move by morning. It costs a season of faith, and nobody is careless again.
The friend goes back into the dark. {npc} does not look at you for an age.

events.text: {npc} has been invited to sit on a jury of the Heavenly Court: three gods judging whether a river may change its course. It is a great honour, it would take a hundred years, and every god on the jury would be watching {him} as closely as {he} watches them.

effects.log: {npc} accepts, glowing. The river gets its new course, and you get a century of the Court's gossip.
{npc} declines, and the honour goes to a rival. {He} does the work, and sulks.

events.text: Your listeners watched {npc} for a season: how {he} moves weather when angry, how far {his} domain reaches before it thins, how long {he} can stand in two worlds at once. It comes as a hymn, each verse a measurement. You know now how strong {npc} truly is.

choices.text: Learn the hymn and burn it

effects.log: It is on {npc}'s page in your People list now, and nowhere else.
You keep it. It has a good tune, which is unsettling for a list of weaknesses.

events.text: "{npc} practises in a dead world where nobody prays," the report says, "so that nobody sees. The power {he} shows the pantheon is a polite one. What {he} practises is not."

effects.log: You know what {npc} really carries.
You stand on its grey shore one morning. You can still feel where {npc} stood.

events.text: The second report on {npc} is about what {he} wants: the gods {he} trusts, the slights {he} has kept since the first age, the world where {he} secretly answers prayers and tells nobody. There is a verse about you. It is fair.

effects.log: You know {npc} better than {his} own pantheon does.
You skip it. You read it later, alone, more than once.

events.text: Your listener brings the report on {npc} in person, which listeners never do. "{He} has been asking at the Book of Fates where your page is kept," they say, "and who reads it, and whether a page can be torn."

choices.text: Move your page to another shelf

effects.log: It costs a favour from a librarian god. {npc} keeps asking, at the wrong shelf.
You sit in {npc}'s hall and admire {his} ceiling for an hour. {He} understands perfectly.

events.text: The last report on {npc} is the one heaven itself was never meant to see. Your listener hands it over in a box of lead, as if it might shine. Everything {npc} has hidden since the worlds were young is inside.

effects.log: A secret kept can still be sold, or used, or forgiven. You keep your choices in a lead box.

choices.text: Burn it after the first line

effects.log: You burn it. You remember the first line anyway, for an age.

events.text: Your listeners have found the thing {npc} would give a domain to keep quiet. They lay it before you and wait, because what they really came to hear tonight is what kind of head they serve.

choices.text: Say nothing will be done with it, yet

effects.log: They nod. Gods have great respect for the word yet.
They smile. Now they know what kind of house this is.

events.text: Your listeners come back from {inw_house} smelling of incense and old stone, its halls mapped in hymn-verse: who quarrels, which domains it truly holds, which elder walks the dark between worlds. The last verse is a door nobody could open, very deep, and behind it something breathing in its sleep, slow as a tide.

effects.log: It goes in the ledger chest under the house's name. The last verse you read three times.

choices.text: Ask how old the breathing sounded

effects.log: "Older than the house," your listener says. "Older than the door."

events.text: The gate-gods of {inw_house} were easy. Its archivist was not: a god of filing with six arms and no sense of humour, who chased your listener across four worlds. The records came out anyway, every page copied into a dream.

effects.log: Your listener spends it on a long sleep, and wakes cheerful.

choices.text: Ask whether the archivist saw a face

effects.log: "Saw a prayer," your listener says. "Not a face."

events.text: From outside, {inw_house} is all splendour and ancient worship. From inside, your listener reports, it is three branches who have not spoken since a sea dried up, a treasury of faith that is mostly promises, and a throne at the back of the hall that nobody sits on and everybody bows to.

choices.text: Ask who the throne is kept for

effects.log: Nobody in the house will say. They lower their voices near it, as if it might wake.
A house that bows to an empty throne is a house waiting for someone. You note it.

events.text: Your listener spent an age as a candle in the ancestral hall of {inw_house}, which is the kind of thing gods can do. The dossier smells of wax: the quarrels, the debts of faith, the worlds it quietly lost. Every night, it says, the eldest of the house kneels at a bare stone floor and speaks to whoever is asleep beneath it.

effects.log: It goes into the ledger chest. You read the last page by candlelight, which feels rude.
"Not yet," your listener says. "Every night, for an age. Just: not yet."

events.text: Heaven keeps a ranking of the mightiest gods, sung at every feast, and every god pretends not to care where they stand in it. Your listeners spent an age testing the names: the war god who has not won since the second age, the quiet goddess ranked fortieth who once moved a mountain range out of spite.

effects.log: You could sing it now. You never will.

choices.text: Keep it for a bad age

effects.log: It goes in the chest. One of those names will come for you some day.

events.text: A choir of young gods sings the ranking at a feast, every place wrong, and the gods named in it applaud themselves. Your listener hums the true order under the music, and stops when a war god glances over.

effects.log: It is a fine choir, even if it is a lie.
The hall goes quiet. The god you corrected will remember you by morning.

events.text: {npc} sits beside you on the steps of the Heavenly Court and sets a jar of prayers between you, then a second. "I want {inw_house}," {he} says. "Its halls, its quarrels, its faith. Not the hymns it pays to have sung. The truth."

effects.log: {npc} lets go of them. "One age," {he} says. "No more."
{npc} takes them back without a flicker. "There are other listeners," {he} says.
"I may marry into it," {npc} says, "or dry up its sea. I have not decided which."

events.text: A dream arrives from {npc}, who does not come in person. In it a voice asks for the inner state of {inw_house} and names a price in faith that no honest god would offer. You wake holding a feather that was not there before.

effects.log: You fall asleep on purpose and say one word. By morning the feather is gone.
You sleep a dreamless sleep. Some prayers are best left unanswered.

events.text: {npc} is back, pleased with the last work, and wants {inw_house} this time, for a little more faith. "I like listeners who hear what they are paid for," {he} says, "and forget who paid."

effects.log: {npc} pays half in advance, as before.

choices.text: Say your listeners are busy this age

effects.log: {npc} shrugs. "Next age, then."

events.text: You hand {npc} the dossier wrapped in a plain prayer cloth. {He} reads the first page standing in the Court, then has to sit on the steps to read the rest while greater gods walk around {him}. When {he} looks up, the weather changes in three worlds.

choices.text: Do not ask what {he} will do

effects.log: {npc} pays the rest, and a little more for your silence.
"Better you do not know," {npc} says, "since you know everything else."

events.text: {npc} pays the second half at a feast, one prayer at a time, loudly, so every god at the table sees that {inw_net} keeps its word.

effects.log: Half the feast will want a contract with you by the next age.

choices.text: Count it again in front of {him}

effects.log: {npc} laughs, and the feast laughs with {him}. Nobody will cheat you soon.

events.text: A thing only your own listeners knew is being sung in a feast hall by a choir of minor gods: a client's name, the price, the domain. Someone in your house is selling. Every face at the morning meeting looks patient, divine and perfectly capable of it.

effects.log: You watch. The one who sold watches back, and you cannot tell which one it is.
It costs a season of faith. The leak stops, for a while.

events.text: A prayer arrives that nobody should have sent: the name of your last client, the price you charged, and at the end, very politely, amen. Somebody wanted you to know that they know. It was not a threat. It was a receipt.

effects.log: You let it go. You count your listeners again that night.
You follow it through four worlds and find a shrine that is not yours, still warm.

events.text: {npc} does not deny it. {He} sits in your back room with {his} hands open on the table. "They said they would strike my name from the Book of Fates," {he} says. "Maybe they could. I did not know who to ask."

effects.log: {npc} stands, bows once, and walks out into the dark with nothing.
{npc} puts {his} head on the table and does not lift it for a long time.

choices.text: Keep {him} selling, and write what {he} sells

effects.log: {npc} understands at once, and goes very pale for a god.

events.text: You lay the copied prayers before {npc} in the order {he} sold them, an age of them. {He} watches the pile grow and smiles at the end. "I always wondered how long you would take," {he} says. "Longer than a mortal. Shorter than a god."

effects.log: {npc} goes laughing, which is somehow worse.
"Of course," {npc} says. "I sing for whoever is winning."
{npc} stops smiling. Forgiveness was the one thing {he} had not priced.

events.text: Your listener at the Third Gate does not report. The gate is quiet, and the Book of Fates lies open at a blank line where their name used to be, with the rival's mark in the margin. Gods are hard to end. They are easy enough to take somewhere no prayer reaches.

choices.text: Search the Book page by page

effects.log: You search a season and find one margin note and nothing else. Your listeners saw you search, and remember.
Your listeners hear you swear. They work harder after that, and far more carefully.

events.text: You wake to the smell of burning incense, far too much of it. By the time you reach your shrine it is ash and a melted bell: an age of listening, a vault of faith, your hymns of record. The fire touched nothing else in that world. Whoever lit it was careful.

effects.log: You borrow a new shrine before the ash is cold. Your listeners see that you do not run.
You wait until the heat passes and heaven forgets the smell of smoke.

events.text: At a feast of the Heavenly Court something quick and cold finds the space under your arm and is gone before you turn. A warning, placed to the hair. Around you the feast goes on. Nobody saw anything, which in heaven is a very loud thing.

effects.log: You raise your cup with the other hand, so whoever is watching sees you keep feasting.
You do not leave your domain for a season.

events.text: {npc}, who speaks for the Oracles of the Silent Hall, sends you a mirror. In it you see your network a long time from now: the shrine empty, the lamp out. The Oracles do not threaten. They simply remember the future at you. From tonight they are listening to your people, and doing worse.

effects.log: {npc} keeps it, which means war anyway, but a courteous one.
The whole Silent Hall hears it, which is saying something.

events.text: Every crossroads in a thousand worlds stops passing your prayers at once. On the last one a toll-box sits open with a note from {npc}: the Choir of the Crossroads has raised your toll to everything. You have been priced.

choices.text: Pay one prayer, the old toll exactly

effects.log: {npc} hears of it and laughs. The war starts anyway, a little friendlier.

choices.text: Kick the toll-box into the dark

effects.log: It falls a long way. Every road spirit in heaven hears it land.

events.text: Your shrine is full of ravens in the morning, hundreds, silent on every beam, and one carries a slip from {npc}: the Throne of Storms has weighed your network and found it heavier than it likes. Outside, the weather has turned against you in eleven worlds.

choices.text: Open the doors and work as usual

effects.log: Your listeners see the doors open, ravens and all, and stay.

choices.text: Close the shutters for a season

effects.log: You work in the dark for a season. It is at least dry.

events.text: The quiet war with {inw_foe} goes on: a prayer that never arrives, a crossroads gone silent, a hymn of yours sung wrong on purpose in a feast hall. {npc} sends no dreams now. Heaven waits to see what you do this age.

effects.log: You give the order.

choices.text: Send {npc} faith and ask for peace

effects.log: You send the faith.

choices.text: Try to turn one of their listeners

ok.log: You find one who will listen.

fail.log: The listener you approach goes straight to {npc}.

events.text: {npc} meets you at midday at the foot of a pantheon's throne, the one place in heaven no network strikes. {He} offers you a fig from a world that grows only one a year. "We could both stop," {he} says. "Or go on until one of us is only a rumour."

choices.text: Eat the fig, and agree a price

effects.log: You name a price. {npc} names a higher one. You pay it.
"Then go on," {npc} says, and eats it, slowly.

events.text: Your listeners bring you the name of {npc}'s best ear: the goddess who weaves robes for half the pantheons and hears every word said at a fitting. The one world that worships the weaver is dying of drought, and the weaver cannot afford the rain.

choices.text: Buy the weaver's world its rain

effects.log: The drought ends. The weaver starts weaving your notes into the hems.
You give the order. You do not rest well for an age.

events.text: It ends at a feast. The spymaster of {inw_foe} pours you a cup of nectar, sets it down and leaves without drinking. {inw_net} has won the quiet war, and every crossroads in heaven is humming it by nightfall.

effects.log: It is excellent. Nobody poisons nectar at a feast all heaven is watching.

choices.text: Leave it, and pay for both cups

effects.log: The feast sees you pay. That is how heaven learns who won.

events.text: You count your listeners at the morning meeting and it takes no time at all. {inw_foe} has the stairs of prayer now, and the crossroads, and one of your shrines with your lamp still in its window. Gods do not forget. Neither, you remind yourself, do you.

effects.log: You start again. The best networks are always smaller than they look.
Your remaining listeners hear you swear it.

events.text: Nobody in heaven says the war with {inw_foe} is over. The prayers simply start arriving again, and the shrines stop burning. It is the kind of peace counted in ages without anyone going quiet.

effects.log: You count the first age. It is a good one.

choices.text: Send their spymaster a jar of honey

effects.log: The jar comes back empty, washed, with a fig in it. It is a reply.

events.text: {npc} holds the empty mirror of {inw_net} the way you held it on the first night: far too carefully, as if it might show {him} something. "Where do I begin?" {he} asks.

effects.log: {npc} laughs, and you hear the head of a network in it.

choices.text: Tell {him}: forget what the mirror showed of me

effects.log: {npc} does not promise. That is how you know you chose well.
